limits: Draft general description, not yet scientifically reviewed. Effectiveness is site-specific and depends on local conditions, design and monitoring.

elements.name: Coral reef
elements.def: Structurally complex limestone habitat built by reef-building corals.
elements.eco: Dissipates wave energy and shelters fish and invertebrates.
elements.methods: Cover surveys, bleaching and disease monitoring, restoration where feasible.
elements.client: Reef condition informs shoreline exposure and asset risk.

elements.name: Seagrass meadow
elements.def: Submerged flowering plants forming meadows in shallow sediment.
elements.eco: Stabilizes sediment, shelters juvenile fish and stores carbon.
elements.methods: Shoot density surveys, habitat mapping, protection or replanting where feasible.
elements.client: Healthier meadows support water quality and shoreline stability.

elements.name: Mangrove
elements.def: Salt-tolerant trees whose root systems stand in tidal water.
elements.eco: Buffers shorelines, traps sediment and provides nursery habitat.
elements.methods: Canopy and root surveys, hydrology assessment, protection or planting.
elements.client: Supports shoreline buffering and habitat obligations.

elements.name: Salt marsh
elements.def: Tidal wetland dominated by salt-tolerant grasses and herbs.
elements.eco: Slows water, traps sediment and filters runoff.
elements.methods: Vegetation transects, elevation and tide monitoring.
elements.client: Possible natural buffer for low-lying property.

elements.name: Beach and dune
elements.def: Sand shoreline and the vegetated ridge behind it.
elements.eco: Absorbs wave energy and holds sand supply for storms.
elements.methods: Beach profiling, vegetation surveys, shoreline mapping.
elements.client: Maintains usable shoreline and protects assets behind it.

elements.name: Coral propagation and outplanting
elements.def: Growing coral fragments or recruits in nurseries, then attaching them to degraded reef.
elements.eco: Adds coral colonies where natural recovery is limited.
elements.methods: Nursery husbandry, outplanting, survival and growth monitoring.
elements.client: Targeted reef recovery with trackable outcomes.

elements.name: Reef structures
elements.def: Engineered substrates placed on the seabed to support reef growth and habitat.
elements.eco: Add physical complexity and habitat, and interact with wave energy.
elements.methods: Design and siting studies, installation, biological and structural monitoring.
elements.client: Combines habitat gain with a possible shoreline-protection function, subject to site engineering.

elements.name: Passive restoration
elements.def: Removing stressors so ecosystems recover without direct planting.
elements.eco: Relies on natural recruitment and recovery.
elements.methods: Stressor assessment, protection measures, long-term monitoring.
elements.client: Lower-intervention baseline for comparison with active options.

elements.name: Active restoration
elements.def: Direct action to rebuild habitat, such as planting, transplanting or placing substrate.
elements.eco: Speeds recovery where natural processes are limited.
elements.methods: Site assessment, restoration works, performance monitoring.
elements.client: Faster, measurable recovery where justified.

elements.name: Hybrid approach
elements.def: Combining engineered structures with living habitat restoration.
elements.eco: Pairs physical stability with ecological function.
elements.methods: Integrated design, staged installation, joint engineering and ecological monitoring.
elements.client: Balances protection performance and ecological value.

elements.name: Conventional infrastructure (comparison)
elements.def: Hard engineering such as seawalls or revetments, used here as a comparison baseline. Not shown in the illustration.
elements.eco: Protects locally but can alter sediment and habitat.
elements.methods: Lifecycle cost comparison, performance and impact review.
elements.client: Enables side-by-side comparison with nature-based options.

elements.name: Drone survey
elements.def: Aerial platform for imaging and surveying coastal areas.
elements.eco: Captures shoreline and habitat extent across large areas.
elements.methods: Repeat flights, orthomosaics, change detection.
elements.client: Low-footprint baseline and progress mapping.

elements.name: Photogrammetry mapping
elements.def: Building measured 3D models and maps from overlapping photographs.
elements.eco: Quantifies reef structure and shoreline form, and how they change.
elements.methods: Overlapping image capture, ground control, model comparison over time.
elements.client: Visual, measurable evidence of change for reporting.

elements.name: Hydrodynamic modeling
elements.def: Numerical models of waves, currents and water levels.
elements.eco: Shows how reefs and habitats affect wave energy and flow.
elements.methods: Field measurements, calibration and validation, scenario runs.
elements.client: Informs design and exposure scenarios, with stated uncertainty.

elements.name: Sensors and loggers
elements.def: Instruments recording conditions such as temperature, waves and water quality.
elements.eco: Tracks environmental drivers that affect habitats.
elements.methods: Deployment, calibration, maintenance, data quality checks.
elements.client: Continuous data for monitoring and reporting.

elements.name: Coral cover
elements.def: The share of seabed covered by living coral.
elements.eco: A common indicator of reef condition.
elements.methods: Photo quadrats, transects, image analysis.
elements.client: A trackable metric for reef recovery.

elements.name: Biodiversity survey
elements.def: A survey of the species present in a habitat.
elements.eco: Indicates habitat function and community recovery.
elements.methods: Visual census, standardized surveys, repeat sampling.
elements.client: Evidence of ecological outcomes beyond physical structure.

elements.name: Wave attenuation
elements.def: Reduction in wave energy as waves cross reefs or vegetation.
elements.eco: A key link between habitat and shoreline protection.
elements.methods: Paired wave sensors, hydrodynamic modeling.
elements.client: Connects habitat to protection performance.

elements.name: Shoreline change
elements.def: Movement of the shoreline position over time.
elements.eco: Shows erosion or accretion trends.
elements.methods: Repeat surveys, drone and satellite imagery, beach profiles.
elements.client: A basis for tracking asset exposure.

elements.name: Coastal protection
elements.def: Reduced wave exposure, flooding or erosion supplied by natural or hybrid features.
elements.eco: Arises from habitats and structures working together.
elements.methods: Wave and shoreline monitoring, modeling.
elements.client: Protection of property and infrastructure, to be quantified for each site.

elements.name: Fisheries support
elements.def: The contribution of habitats to fish and invertebrate populations.
elements.eco: Habitats provide nursery and feeding grounds.
elements.methods: Fish surveys, catch data where available.
elements.client: Livelihood and food-security benefits for communities.

elements.name: Asset and property value
elements.def: Economic value of coastal property and infrastructure tied to shoreline condition.
elements.eco: Depends on protection, access and setting.
elements.methods: Exposure assessment, valuation, damage and maintenance records.
elements.client: Avoided losses and maintenance costs, to be modeled with verified inputs.

elements.name: Blue carbon
elements.def: Carbon stored in coastal vegetated habitats and their sediments.
elements.eco: Mangroves, marsh and seagrass can hold carbon in soils.
elements.methods: Sediment coring, habitat mapping, accounting methods.
elements.client: A possible carbon-finance pathway, subject to methodology and verification.
